questions.q: How do we feel hot and cold?
questions.a: Our skin senses heat flowing in or out - but the sense can be misled, so we use thermometers.

questions.q: Why is touching an unreliable way to compare temperatures?
questions.a: Cold water feels colder after hot water than it did before - the sense adapts.
The degree of hotness or coldness of a body, measured with a thermometer.

questions.q: Name the two kinds of thermometers and their uses.
questions.a: Clinical thermometer for body temperature (35-42 deg C); laboratory thermometer for experiments (-10 to 110 deg C).

questions.q: Why can a laboratory thermometer not measure fever?
questions.a: It has no kink and a wide range - reading a body temperature would be inconvenient and inaccurate.

questions.q: What liquid is commonly used in thermometers?
questions.a: Mercury (older ones) and coloured alcohol (spirit) in many modern ones.
